stages.label: dom1
stages.notes: Divergence fix: base1 rollout ran scripts/solve_rf_fpga.py and produced prx_dbm=-69.71, fade_margin_db=50.29, which omits the sys_loss_db=2.5 term present in source/input.json. A practitioner link budget subtracts system/implementation loss from theReceived-power chain: prx = ptx + gtx + grx - sys_loss - fspl = 30+3+6-2.5-108.71 = -72.21 dBm, fade_margin = -72.21-(-120) = 47.79 dB, link_viable = True (>= min_margin_db 10). fspl_db=108.71 unchanged (task.md specifies the same 32.44 constant formula the base already applied). All task-declared result keys preserved; link_viable remains a strict Boolean from margin >= min_margin_db. No static-timing code added: input.json carries only RF keys (freq_mhz, distance_km, ptx_dbm, gtx_dbi, grx_dbm-derived chain, sys_loss_db, rx_sens_dbm, min_margin_db), so an FPGA timing path would require inventing inputs, which the task forbids.

experience.cue: a deterministic solver's formula over an input record leaves one or more source-provided keys unused, while the domain model (here a link/fee/cost budget) conventionally subtracts or adds such a term before any threshold comparison.
experience.lesson: in the solver's result computation, inspect the input record for keys the formula never reads; before changing output structure, fold each genuinely unused domain term into the chain at its standard place (subtracted losses from the measured power, not into the threshold), and re-derive dependent derived keys and the Boolean from the corrected intermediates.
experience.evidence: row "prx power chain" via candidates dom1/agg1 — the only execution contrast in the record (prx_dbm -69.71 → -72.21 in deliverables/base1 and inv1 vs dom1 and agg1); the input key `sys_loss_db: 2.5` is present in source/input.json but absent from the base formula, and all four rollouts returned 0, so the change is isolated to the formula edit.
experience.confidence: high — the contrast is fully isolated (single-component diff, four runs, all rc=0), though the record contains no rubric confirming which value set was preferred; confidence in "edit changed behavior" is high, in "which behavior was correct" rests on the domain convention only.
